listenings.text: I have been coaching at this club for nineteen years, and I have seen a lot of kids come through. Most of them stay for one season. He has been with me since he was nine, which is unusual. What I tell parents is always the same thing: nothing happens in the first two years. Nothing. He finished last in his first four events and he did not miss a single training session. Then at fourteen, the podium. People say it happened suddenly. It has been happening slowly since he was nine, and nobody was watching.

We have been teammates since primary school, so about seven years. I have known him longer than anybody at that club except the coach. Honestly, he was not the best one when we started. There were four of us and he was the slowest. But he has not missed a Saturday since I met him, not one, not even the week his leash broke and he had no board. He borrowed mine. For seven years he has been the first one in the water and the last one out, and now he is going to Australia. Fair enough, really.

items.situation: Somebody asks how long you have been surfing. Answer twice: once with for, once with since.
Describe your club: how long you have been there and who else is there.
Name a milestone in your life and say how long ago it was.
Somebody asks how long you have known your best friend. Answer.
Say two things you have NOT done for a long time.

paras: Renato has been surfing since he was eight years old. That is the first milestone, and it is the only one he does not really remember: his father pushed him into a small wave and he stood up by accident.
He has been in the same club since he was nine. Same beach, same coach, same green shirt. The coach has known him for six years now, which is longer than most of his school friends have.

The first competition was at twelve. He finished last, and he has not forgotten it since. Two years later, at fourteen, he stood on the podium for the first time. The trophy has been on the same shelf for a year and a half.

This season he has been in the junior category for the first time, and he has been training three mornings a week since January. In February he leaves for Australia, and that will be the fourth milestone on the list.
